title: How Citibank Lost $900,000,000 With One Click

sources.short: In re Citibank August 11, 2020 Wire Transfers, S.D.N.Y., Feb 16 2021
sources.fact: Citibank meant to wire about $7.8M in interest to Revlon lenders and wired about $893.9M; lenders kept about $504M; judge: one of the biggest blunders in banking history.

scenes.prompt: Cinematic night photo of Manhattan office towers seen from above, a few windows lit, cold blue tones with warm window light, shallow haze, 16:9, moody documentary still, no text

lines.say: On a quiet Tuesday evening a Citibank employee clicks a button to send a routine payment.
It should be about eight million dollars.
Instead the bank wires out almost nine hundred million dollars of its own money.

scenes.prompt: Cinematic 3D render of a huge round steel bank vault door standing open in a dark concrete room, one cold spotlight from above, gold reflections inside, dramatic shadows, 16:9, no text

lines.say: Nobody hacked anything and nobody stole a password.

scenes.head: CITIBANK · AUGUST 11 2020
scenes.source: SOURCE: U.S. DISTRICT COURT, S.D.N.Y. · VALUE AT TIME OF TRANSFER

lines.say: The bank meant to send this much.
And it sent this much which is more than one hundred times too much.

scenes.by: U.S. DISTRICT JUDGE JESSE FURMAN · FEBRUARY 16 2021

lines.say: A federal judge would later call it one of the biggest blunders in banking history.

show.t: one of the biggest blunders in banking history

lines.say: The payment leaves at five forty five.
Nobody notices until the next morning.
The bank asks for the money back and some of the lenders simply say no.
Almost nine hundred million dollars went out.
And about half a billion of it did not come back.
So this is the story of the click and of who kept the money and of what the judge decided.
It starts at five forty five in the evening.
